required_stages.description: Allocate the (N, C) output (empty_like) and the fp32 scratch: per-block partial sums and sums of squares (num_blocks, C) and mean / inv_std (C,).
First read of input: one launch in which each program reduces a contiguous block of rows to per-channel fp32 partial sum and sum of squares (or equivalent single-pass moments) written to scratch.
Per channel, combine the block partials in fp32 into mean and inv_std = rsqrt(max(sumsq/N - mean^2, 0) + eps); may be its own launch or folded into the apply prologue.
Second read of input: y = x*scale + shift with scale = inv_std*gamma, shift = beta - mean*scale in fp32, stored in the input dtype.

forbidden_substitutions.message: A library normalisation replaces the whole computation.
A host-side tensor reduction replaces the statistics stages.
A tensor-method reduction on the host replaces a required device stage.
Atomic accumulation of channel totals replaces the deterministic two-level reduction.
Host-side upcast copies of input/gamma/beta are forbidden; upcast inside the kernels.
Scratch is fully written before it is read; zero-filled buffers are not part of this operator.
Caching statistics or scratch across calls is forbidden.

required_evidence.message: No sum-reduction primitive found; the statistics must be reduced in the kernels.
No rsqrt/sqrt found; inv_std = rsqrt(var + eps) is required.

outputs.aliasing: none; the returned (N, C) tensor must be freshly allocated inside run() and must not share storage with input, gamma or beta

timing_boundary.notes: Everything inside run() is timed: the output and four fp32 scratch allocations, zero-copy views, the partial-statistics launch, the per-channel combine (own launch or folded into apply) and the apply launch. No host-side casts or copies of the inputs; nothing cached across calls.
